title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, is suing Fargo, North Dakota, and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million after being falsely charged with bank theft. She was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 while babysitting four children, then spent nearly four months in a Tennessee jail without bail and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges, four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft, were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud. She was released on Christmas Eve and later found she had lost her home, car, and personal property.

The lawsuit says Fargo police used AI facial recognition that matched Lipps's social media photo to a fake ID from surveillance video. It alleges Detective Heck requested an arrest warrant without further investigation or probable cause, and that the department lacked training and supervision for the technology. Fargo declined to comment. Lipps seeks damages and accountability, hoping to encourage more careful use of facial recognition.
